pages.text: "Grandpa, when will the bread be ready?" Nils the little bear circled the table. Grandpa Bruno was baking bread in the forest cabin stove. A jar of blueberry jam stood in the middle of the table.
"I will spread jam on fresh bread!" Nils swallowed eagerly. Unable to wait, he quietly opened the jar. One spoonful, two spoonfuls, three spoonfuls. "Just a little more, a little more..."
It was evening. Steaming bread lay on a plate, but Nils had such a full tummy that he could not eat a bite. "I want it, but there is no room..." He bowed his head.
Grandpa sat on the stool beside Nils and gently tapped his tummy. "The jam filled your tummy, leaving no room for bread." Nils blinked, and one tear fell.
Grandpa set a spoon beside the jam jar. "Your tummy is a room this size. Fill it with jam, and the bread cannot come in." Nils looked at his bulging belly. The room was full, with no space for bread.
"One spoon is your bowl for jam." Grandpa scooped exactly one spoonful. Nils stared at it. It was much smaller than he had expected. "Just one spoonful of jam!" he repeated.
The next evening, the jam jar was on the table again. Nils put a paw on the lid, then lowered it. "Just one spoonful of jam!" It was hard to wait, but he did it.
Fresh bread arrived. Nils took a big bite of bread first. Yum! Then he spread exactly one spoonful of jam and took another bite. "Did bread always taste this good?" He pushed the jar back.
Holding the spoon, Nils counted. "One, bread first! Two, just one spoonful of jam! Three, Grandpa opens the jar!" Then he lifted both paws high above his head.
Grandpa sat Nils on his lap and patted his back. A little jam makes bread taste better. "Grandpa, tomorrow too—just one spoonful of jam!"
